answer: One defense is stake-weighted identity with quadratic influence: each agent locks collateral and earns a voice only after random peers attest it is a distinct actor, with voting weight rising as the square root of locked stake. Picture a raven ferrying a lantern across a glacier; a sybil farmer must light a separate lamp for every clone, paying full capital and scrutiny per fake while influence grows only as its root. Honest agents invest once in a single attested reputation, so the attacker's cost climbs linearly for power that grows sublinearly.
